digest.lead: Boris Cherny, the creator of Claude Code, gave a candid look at trying to use Claude Code to rewrite Anthropic's own Claude app in Swift — a real-world stress test of how far agentic coding tools can go on a large, gnarly codebase.
digest.summary: Today's news is light, with the Cherny piece as the standout item generating discussion on Hacker News about the practical ceiling of current coding agents on big rewrites.

stories.headline: Claude Code creator Boris Cherny details attempt to rewrite Claude's app with Claude Code
stories.summary: Boris Cherny, who built Claude Code, shared his experience trying to use the tool to rewrite Anthropic's Claude app in Swift [1]. The piece, linked via Daring Fireball, sparked discussion on Hacker News about how well agentic coding tools handle large-scale rewrites of production codebases [1].
key_points: Cherny is a key figure behind Claude Code, giving his account added credibility as a dogfooding case study [1]
The discussion touches on practical limits and successes of using AI agents for substantial rewrites rather than small tasks [1]
stories.impact: This offers developers using Claude Code daily a rare inside look at how Anthropic's own engineers stress-test the tool on real, large-scale rewrites, informing expectations for what agentic coding can and can't yet handle.

stories.headline: Update permission mode references to 'manual' after upgrading Claude Code
stories.summary: The default permission mode across CLI, VS Code, and JetBrains is now called 'Manual' instead of 'default'. Existing configs using 'default' still work, but scripts or docs referencing the old name should be updated for clarity.
actionable_steps: Search your configs and scripts for `--permission-mode default` or `"defaultMode": "default"`
Verify behavior matches expectations in CLI, VS Code, and JetBrains integrations

stories.headline: Use Claude's extended thinking for complex architectural decisions
stories.summary: When asking Claude to make non-trivial design choices — like choosing between patterns, structuring a new module, or planning a migration — enabling extended thinking produces significantly better results. Claude will reason through trade-offs before committing to an approach, catching issues that quick responses miss.
actionable_steps: For architecture questions, ask Claude to 'think through the trade-offs' explicitly
Use Claude Code's plan mode (shift+tab) for multi-step tasks that need careful reasoning
Review Claude's reasoning in extended thinking to catch flawed assumptions early

sources.title: Tips for getting better architectural advice from Claude

stories.headline: Use `claude plugin prune` to clean up orphaned plugin dependencies
stories.summary: Auto-installed plugin dependencies can accumulate over time, taking up disk space. The prune command removes dependencies that are no longer needed by any installed plugins.
actionable_steps: Run `claude plugin prune` in your terminal
Alternatively, use `claude plugin uninstall --prune [plugin-name]` to uninstall a plugin and clean up its dependencies in one step

stories.headline: Use bare /color command to randomize your Claude Code session color
stories.summary: The /color command without arguments now automatically selects a random color for your session. This provides a quick way to visually distinguish different sessions without manually choosing colors.
actionable_steps: Press Enter to apply a random session color

stories.headline: Use the Dynamic Workflow Size setting to control agent counts
stories.summary: Claude Code v2.1.202 adds a 'Dynamic workflow size' option in /config that lets you guide how many agents Claude spawns for dynamic workflows (small/medium/large). This is an advisory setting, not a hard cap, so it helps balance speed vs. thoroughness for multi-agent tasks.
actionable_steps: Set it to small, medium, or large based on task complexity and desired agent count
